title: Helpdesk search-intent boundary research: when similar words need different routes
excerpt: A study of customer wording, search grouping, and the boundary where a shared phrase no longer supports one safe helpdesk answer.
question: Which evidence shows that two similar helpdesk search phrases share an answer, and which evidence shows that their permissions or next actions diverge?
focus: search intent, customer language, and route-specific support boundaries
finding: language can group requests for discovery, but only a matching action, audience, and stopping point justify one answer path
limitation: search terms underrepresent callers, abandoned sessions, and multilingual requests
